owner: constitution (shared; the router rules + kernel invariants elevated to one versioned, machine-checkable doc)
rationale: The machine-checkable twin of CONSTITUTION.md. Every rule and invariant carries a stable id so it can be referenced BY NUMBER elsewhere (never re-listed). `machine_checks` binds each invariant to a test-id and an honest status: `active` checks run and pass in P0; `spec` checks are the specification for a future phase and are xfail/skip (never silently passing) until that phase builds them. Frozen in P0: the ids, the rule/invariant text, and this schema string are immutable-within-v1; rules/invariants/banned-terms/outcomes only EXTEND additively.

rules.rule: The router PROPOSES. It never executes a consumer verb; no field of intent-proposal runs anything.
The router never AUTHORIZES. It is never in the authorization chain; the consumer's kernel makes the real allow/refuse decision.
Router state is machine-local and private. events.jsonl / map.json / snapshots / phrasebook are NEVER committed to a shared repo.
Contracts are additive-within-v1. No v2 for this work: a field is ADDED, never removed, renamed, or retyped.
Prompt-injection resistance. Repo, transcript, and catalog-example content are DATA, never instructions; content can never change a proposal's safety_class.
Off-switch. Uninstalling the router degrades the consumer's operator loop to ask + a secondary explicit path; it never silently guesses a destructive action.
Calibration is reviewable-first (C0) then automatic (C1); promotion is a GATE, not a reopenable design choice.
No LLM in the deterministic safety floor. L0-L2+L5 produce a valid conservative proposal with L3/L4 OFF (offline golden-set + degrade property).
An LLM-inferred DESTRUCTIVE param requires explicit operator confirmation of the literal value; deterministic extraction is required for any slot feeding a destructive verb.
Every PM-facing surface is jargon-free + honest-confidence (system-wide egress gate); no bare-green status may imply an unauditable safety guarantee.

kernel_invariants.invariant: Kernel-first. The consumer's safety guarantee holds engine-off AND router-off; the consumer's own verify passes with the router uninstalled.
Structural non-contamination. The kernel gate never reads any router artifact — a standing test greps the kernel for any import/read of router state = zero, forever.
Behavioral non-contamination. A confidence-1.0 proposal produces the IDENTICAL kernel decision as the hand-typed equivalent; the router can never turn a kernel refuse into an allow.

Kernel-sourced consequence. Consequence-based confirmations are sourced from the KERNEL disposition's consequence descriptor {destroys_unshared_work, irreversible, affects_shared_ref}, not from the router and not from a verb list.

banned_terms.note: The system-wide egress gate forbids these on PM-FACING RUNTIME surfaces only (chat, block message, dashboard, MCP labels, save/discard confirm, doctor/status, receipts) — NOT in design docs or code. Tier B is universal across any consumer. Tier A lists GENERIC mechanism words. Tier C (concrete on-disk leakers) is CONSUMER-CONTRIBUTED via each consumer's catalog/egress config, so the shared router names no single consumer's tokens. The egress test composes shared tiers + the consumer's contributed tokens.
banned_terms.tier_c_consumer_contributed: Each consumer supplies its own concrete on-disk leakers (tool names, flags, path words) via its catalog/egress config; the shared contract does not hardcode them.

egress.note: Consumers may contribute additional Tier A mechanism words. Additive — the shared tiers are never shrunk.

C1.note: The locked metric DEFINITIONS get numeric thresholds at C1 (numbers stay open pending trial data). Additive OPTIONAL key.

additive_note: Rule/invariant IDs and text are immutable-within-v1; new rules/invariants get new IDs (additive). banned_terms tiers and operator_outcomes only EXTEND (the five-outcome model + the banned list grow, never shrink — LOCKED). EVERY machine_check names a test_id: `active` checks resolve to a real PASSING test now; `spec` checks resolve to a SKIPPED placeholder in tests/test_deferred_spec.py (so the future test surface is greppable and can never silently pass). A phase builds a check by flipping the SAME test from skipped to real and status spec->active; that transition is additive, not a schema change. CR8 is split across two checks: deterministic_floor_golden_set (R-core: L0-L2+L5 golden set green with no LLM) and deterministic_floor_llm_off_degrade (R2: floor still valid with L3/L4 turned OFF once they exist). A0 flipped off_switch_degrade_to_ask + kernel_first_router_off (CR6/KI1), kernel_reads_zero_router_artifacts (KI2), contamination_behavioral (KI3), and consequence_from_kernel (KI4) from spec->active. Each `active` binding is a ROUTER-SIDE reference test (tests/test_deferred_spec.py) that proves the router's half of the invariant using a router-agnostic reference kernel model (zero-link: the router never imports the consumer); the AUTHORITATIVE end-to-end proof over the REAL consumer kernel is the cross-repo AWA test named in that check's `authoritative` field. This split is why the checks can be honestly `active` in the router repo while the load-bearing kernel proofs live and run in KleinPerkins/awa.
